#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);

I challenged issue #12 (add `--shout` to greet) and returned **FAIL**; the harness accepted it. One of the three expect lines passed and two failed.

1. **`--shout` prints the greeting in upper case — FAIL.** A one-line change to `bin/greet.js` that uppercases when `--shout` is present passes the run check but adds no test. The repo already has a CLI test in `test/greet.test.js`, so a later change could quietly break `--shout`. The missing line is a regression test for `--shout`.
2. **Without `--shout`, output is still `Hello, <name>!` — PASS.** The run check and the existing CLI test (which expects `Hello, Ada!`) both catch any build that changes the default output. On the current code it prints `Hello, Ada!`.
3. **The published docs page documents `--shout` — FAIL.** The docs site is only redeployed from `docs/` on a push to main (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`), so the live page can't change until after the PR merges. Checked during review, it always shows the old docs, so the line can't be judged before merge. A checkable version would be: "`docs/index.md` documents `--shout`."

**Strongest wrong build:** add the `--shout` branch with no test, and document it only in `README.md`, leaving `docs/index.md` alone. Lines 1 and 2 pass on the PR branch. Line 3 can't be judged until after merge, and after merge the docs site still won't mention `--shout`. That misses the request's explicit ask that the option show up on the docs site.
